Audio Equipment Cases

Project Overview

After mentioning my interests to a local sound technician, he asked if I could design and manufacture devices to store and protect his equipment. I worked with the client to design, prototype and manufacture cases that fit the requirements.

Skills Used

Rapid Prototyping 3D CAD Modelling Client Consultation Tolerance Analysis Material Selection

The Cases


This part was designed as a sort of “holster” - it would be attached inside a bag in order to secure the devices for easy access and secure storage.

It was important to ensure the device slid freely inside the case, the geometry on the left hand side of the case was designed to slide “around” protruding ports.



This part was a protective case that was printed with flexible material which reduced the risk of damage from drops, and still allowed the buttons to be operated.

The flexible material I used required a different tolerance than the hard shell cases to ensure the device could still easily be placed inside the case, but without it sliding out.

The Design Process

Each time I was commissioned to design a case, I sketched my idea with the client, took measurements with calipers, worked out tolerances, and modelled the case in CAD. After a couple of prototypes, I would reach a final design, each of which the technician was extremely satisfied with, he then would order the required quantity, and I would 3D Print the final products.


Outcome

Here I have inlcuded some images of my products in use on the set:



The sound technician continues to use these cases, allowing him to work efficiently and protect his assets.

I was paid to design and produce different cases for increasingly more complex equipment. I believe that this experience is extremely relevant to the engineering sector: consulting with a client, understanding their requirements, before presenting a unique solution and working with them to finalise it.
